The War Is Over. Mind the Missiles.

Trump says the Iran conflict is “militarily, effectively over.” U.S. forces are still striking Iranian positions on Qeshm Island, and Tehran says it has attacked Didamar, an Omani islet whose navigation equipment guides ships through Hormuz.

U.S. and Gulf officials told The Wall Street Journal that the Qeshm strikes aim to stop Iranian missile and drone attacks on shipping. Washington calls them limited defensive operations, not preparation for a major assault.

Iranian state television said Didamar’s navigation equipment was helping the enemy “smuggle” oil. An Omani coast guard official confirmed an explosion but gave no details. Tehran now treats equipment that helps ships find their way as hostile infrastructure.

The U.S. blockade also continues. Over the weekend, U.S. aircraft attacked the cargo ship Huda, and Emirati forces rescued its 22 crew members. CENTCOM says American forces have disabled five ships during the blockade.

Washington wants Iranian trade stopped while other Gulf exports keep moving, and Tehran wants passage through Hormuz on its terms. Neither side needs a new bombing campaign to keep fighting over who may sail.

Major combat may be over, but for the crews caught between the blockade and the missiles, that distinction offers little protection.
